textbookText: 1. Action with air

Figure: Burning Magnesium ribbon in air When alkaline earth metals are exposed to atmosphere, then they become dull as a layer of oxide is formed. 2Mg + O2 → 2MgO (magnesium oxide) 2Ca + O2 → 2CaO (calcium oxide) Note: Be is much less affected by air.
Test Yourself! Why does magnesium ribbon get tarnished when exposed in atmosphere for long time?

2. Action with water Alkaline earth metals react with water to produce alkali and hydrogen gas except Be. 2Ca + 2H2O → Ca(OH)2 + H2 2Ba + 2H2O → Ba(OH)2 + H2 2Sr + 2H2O → Sr(OH)2 + H2 Mg reacts only on boiling,
⎯⎯→ Mg + 2H2O Boil Mg(OH)2 + H2
Figure: calcium metal in water
Test Yourself! What happens when a piece of magnesium ribbon is kept in boiling water?
CHEMISTRY, GRADE 11 | 508

3. Action with Hydrogen Except Be, all alkaline earth metals react with hydrogen to produce their corresponding hydrides. Mg + H2 →MgH2 (magnesium hydride) Ca + H2 →CaH2 (calcium hydride) Ba+ H2 →BaH2 (barium hydride)
Test Yourself! How does Sr react with hydrogen gas?
4. Action with Nitrogen Alkaline earth metals react with nitrogen at high temperature to form their corresponding nitride. 3Mg + N2 → Mg3N2 (magnesium nitride) 3Ca + N2 → Ca3N2 (calcium nitride)
Test Yourself! What happens when Mg ribbon is heated with nitrogen gas?
5. Action with acids

Activity-8 Take a beaker containing some dilute sulphuric acid and to this acid add a piece of magnesium ribbon. Observe the reaction and answer the following questions. a. Name the gas evolved. b. Write the balanced chemical reaction.

Alkaline earth metals react with mineral acids to produce hydrogen gas. Mg + HCl → MgCl2 + H2 Ca + H2SO4 → CaSO4 + H2 Note: Be reacts with acid with most common acids (except HNO3) more vigorously such that the reacting vessel has to be kept in an ice bath.
6. Action with non-metals: Alkaline earth metals react with non-metals like halogens, sulphur, phosphorous, carbon, etc. as Mg + Cl2 → MgCl2 (magnesium chloride)
Ca + P→ Ca3P2 (calcium phosphide) Ba + S → BaS (barium sulphide)

10.3.2: Molecular formula and uses of some compounds of alkaline earth metals
List of some important compounds of alkaline earth metals are listed below:
1. Quick Lime Calcium oxide is commonly known as quicklime or burnt lime. Its molecular formula is CaO. In Nepali
it is called chuna.
Uses of quick lime Some uses of quick lime are listed below:
a. It is used in the manufacture of calcium carbide (CaC2) and bleaching powder.

b. It is a raw material for the preparation of cement. c. It is used in the preparation of soda lime (NaOH + CaO). d. It is used in the manufacture of glass, washing soda etc, e. It is a basic flux in metallurgy. f. It is used as a dehydrating agent for drying gases, alcohols and other
compounds. g. It is used as a fertilizer.
Figure: Quick lime
2. Bleaching powder Calcium chlorohypochlorite is commonly known as bleaching powder. Its molecular formula is
CaOCl2. It is also known as chloride of lime or chlorinated lime.
Uses of bleaching powder Some uses of bleaching powder are listed below:
a. It is used in the manufacture of chloroform. b. It is used to bleach paper, pulp, cotton, linen goods, etc. c. It is used as a disinfectant. In the presence of moisture it releases

kills germs and disinfects the area. d. It is in sterilizing drinking water. e. It is used as an oxidizing agent. f. It is used to whiten clothes and remove stains. g. It is used to clean old items like jewellery items or showpieces.

3. Magnesia Magnesium oxide is chemically known as magnesia. Its molecular formula is MgO.
Uses of magnesia Some uses of magnesia are listed below:
CHEMISTRY, GRADE 11 | 510

a. It is used as refractory material in lining of furnaces, bricks etc due to its high melting point. b. It is used in the manufacture of cement. c. It is used to prepare crucible. d. Its aqueous suspension is called milk of magnesia which is used for treating constipation (laxative). e. It is used as an antacid for curing gastritis. f. It is used as a basic flux in metallurgy.
Figure: Milk of magnesia 4. Plaster of paris Calcium sulphate hemihydrate is chemically known as plaster of paris. Its molecular formula is CaSO4.1/2 H2O.
Uses of plaster of paris Some uses of plaster of paris are listed below:

a. It is used for setting fractured and broken bones in the body. b. It is used for making statues, models and various decorative items. c. It is used as a fireproofing materials and also used for making chalks
to write. d. It is used in making artificial marbles and false-ceiling. e. It is used in construction of buildings to fill small gaps on the walls and roofs.
Figure: use of Plaster of paris for setting fractured bones
5. Epsom salt Magnesium sulphate heptahydrate is chemically known as plaster of Epsom salt.
Its molecular formula is MgSO4.7H2O.
